newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestries extend rally on strong Helsinki bourse.
newsitem.headline: Forestries extend rally on strong Helsinki bourse.

text.p: Finnish shares rose in upbeat mood on Monday, cheered by Wall Street's gains last week and by a rally in forestry shares which started on Thursday in Sweden and spread to Finland, brokers said.
The HEX index set a new intra-session life-high of 2,342.66, -- 9.8 points above its previous high from last week, but closed slightly off but still at a closing life-high of 2,430.9.
Nokia was relatively quiet with less than 15 percent of the volume. It closed up 1.00 at 258.00 markka.

"There seems to be incredible belief in this market," one broker said. "But we are dangerously high. A downturn could come easily, but it would take some outside impetus such as new (economic) figures from the U.S.," he added.
Brokers said the forestry boom was unlikely to be just end-year window-dressing. "It wouldn't pay to start brushing up the figures a whole month before the year ends," said one.
Europe's largest forestry group UPM-Kymmene rose 0.90 markka to close at 93.20 and the forestry index added 1.63 percent to 2,110.0 points.

Shares in national carrier Finnair and diversified engineering group Metra rose after both announced the sale of their hotel buildings at small profits to a new company owned by the two and state alcohol monopoly Alko's parent company.
Kesko pared some of the losses that have recently followed the EU's ban of its merger with Tuko, rising 1.50 to 63.20 markka in lively 14 million markka trade.
